# Notely

A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind.

## Status

- Auth is handled by [Better Auth](https://better-auth.com) — email + password and Google sign-in.
- Users, sessions and OAuth accounts live in a local SQLite file (`notely.db`), reached through `src/lib/users.ts`.
- `/dashboard` is protected: anonymous visitors get bounced to `/sign-in`.
- There is no billing and no email (password reset and verification are off).

## Develop

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local   # fill in the Google credentials to use Google sign-in
npm run dev
```

The auth tables are created on server start by `src/instrumentation.ts`, so there is no separate migrate step. Delete `notely.db` to start from an empty user list.

## How auth is wired

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/lib/auth.ts` | Better Auth server instance and config |
| `src/lib/auth-client.ts` | Browser client (`signIn`, `signUp`, `signOut`, `useSession`) |
| `src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` | Mounts every auth endpoint under `/api/auth` |
| `src/lib/users.ts` | App-facing user reads: `listUsers`, `getUser`, `getCurrentUser`, `requireUser` |
| `src/proxy.ts` | Redirects anonymous requests for `/dashboard` before they render |
| `src/instrumentation.ts` | Runs schema migrations on boot |

Route protection is two-layered: `src/proxy.ts` does a cheap session-cookie check, and `requireUser()` inside the page validates the session against the database on every request. Adding a page to the protected set means adding its path to the matcher in `src/proxy.ts` and calling `requireUser()` in it.

### Google sign-in

Create an OAuth client at <https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials> and register `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google` as an authorized redirect URI. Without real credentials the button still renders and redirects, but Google rejects the placeholder client ID.

**Choice: Better Auth + SQLite.** Self-hosted (no external service to sign up for), TypeScript-native, email/password with scrypt hashing and Google OAuth built in, and it works today with placeholder credentials. Auth.js would have needed a custom credentials provider plus a separate adapter for signup; Clerk/Supabase would have made the app unrunnable without real accounts.

**What's there**
- `src/lib/auth.ts` — server config: email+password (min 8 chars, auto sign-in), Google provider, 30-day sessions.
- `src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` — all auth endpoints under `/api/auth`.

- `src/lib/users.ts` — same `User` shape and function names, now reading the Better Auth `user` table; `getCurrentUser()` resolves the real session instead of `users[0]`. Added `requireUser()`, which the dashboard uses so protection doesn't rest on the proxy alone.
- `src/instrumentation.ts` — creates the tables on boot, so `npm run dev` works with no migrate step.
- `.env.example` with placeholders (and `.gitignore` fixed — its `.env*` rule was swallowing the example file).

**Verified with curl:** anonymous `/dashboard` → 307 to `/sign-in?next=/dashboard`; sign-up creates a user; the dashboard then renders "Signed in as Ada (ada@example.com)" with the team list from the DB; wrong password → 401; Google returns a correct PKCE auth URL; sign-out clears the session and `/dashboard` bounces again; `?next=//evil.example.com` is neutralized; cross-origin sign-out → 403. `npm run build` and `npm run lint` pass.

Two things worth your call: I dropped `@better-auth/cli` because it pulls in 8 vulnerable transitive deps (chevrotain/lodash) — migrations run at boot instead, which is fine for SQLite but you'd want an explicit migrate step on a shared Postgres. And email verification and password reset are off, since there's no mail sending in the project yet.
